name: Yaoko Kawagoe Museum
key_features: A Kawagoe art museum showing the works of Western-style painter Misu Yuji.

name: Bing Concert Hall
key_features: A Stanford concert hall with 842 seats in vineyard-style terraces around the stage, by Richard Olcott of Ennead Architects.

name: Church of the Three Crosses
key_features: Nave divides into three with sliding walls, under curved acoustic ceilings and double windows.

name: Munich Olympic Stadium
key_features: Cable-net roof with acrylic glass panels; seating set into an earth-bowl landscape.

name: CaixaForum Madrid
key_features: A brick power station cut free at its base so it floats over a shaded plaza, beside a vertical garden.

name: National Museum of Roman Art
key_features: Parallel brick walls pierced by tall arches form a top-lit nave above excavated Roman ruins.

name: 122 Leadenhall Street
key_features: A tapering tower held by an exposed perimeter megaframe, with cores and lifts pushed to the north.

name: Van Gogh Museum
key_features: Open central hall with stairs under skylights links the galleries on every floor.

name: Art Tower Mito
key_features: A 100 m tower of stacked titanium tetrahedra twists as a helix above an arts complex plaza.

name: Arctic Cathedral
key_features: Stepped triangular panels form a tall A-frame, with a large stained-glass east wall.

name: Church of St Joan of Arc
key_features: Swooping slate roof like an upturned hull, set with 16th-century stained glass from a lost church.

name: Cidade das Artes
key_features: Concert halls held between two horizontal concrete slabs above a raised public terrace.

name: Gallery of Modern Art
key_features: Thin flat roof floating over glazed galleries and a deep shaded verandah facing the river.

name: Olympic Stadium, Ciudad Universitaria de Caracas
key_features: Grandstand sheltered by cantilevered concrete canopies, part of a campus uniting art and architecture.

name: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni
key_features: Unfinished palazzo on the Grand Canal, only its low ground floor built, now a gallery.

name: Australian National Maritime Museum
key_features: Waterfront halls under curved steel roofs that evoke sails and wave forms.

name: Dentsu Building (Caretta Shiodome)
key_features: Slim curved glass tower whose fritted glass shifts in tone up its height to dissolve into the sky.

name: Aurora Place
key_features: Curving tower whose glass facade extends past its edges and roof as free-standing sails.

name: Church of Saint-Nicolas, Hérémence
key_features: A craggy cluster of rough concrete volumes rises like a rock outcrop above the mountain village.

name: Scharoun Theatre Wolfsburg
key_features: Fan-shaped auditorium and flowing, asymmetric foyer levels in Scharoun's organic plan.

name: Ara Pacis Museum
key_features: A white travertine, plaster and glass pavilion encloses the Augustan altar in a daylit glass hall.

name: Capitol Records Building
key_features: A round tower ringed by projecting sunshade fins and topped by a spire, often likened to a stack of records.

name: Casa Bloc
by: Josep Lluís Sert, Josep Torres Clavé and Joan Baptista Subirana
key_features: Duplex flats in long slabs on pilotis, reached by open access galleries, wind around shared gardens.

name: Cathedral of Learning
key_features: A limestone Gothic Revival skyscraper rising from a vast vaulted hall, the Commons Room.

name: Cuvilliés Theatre
key_features: Rococo court theatre of carved, gilded wooden tiers, dismantled in the war and reinstalled in the Residenz.

name: Entebbe Children's Surgical Hospital
key_features: Rammed-earth walls under a raised roof of solar panels that shades the wards and powers the hospital.

name: McGregor Memorial Conference Center
key_features: White travertine pavilion with a skylit atrium, triangulated concrete ceilings and a reflecting pool.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport Terminal 2
key_features: Coffered roof on tall mushroom columns, pierced by skylights in a peacock-feather pattern.

name: Baitul Mukarram
key_features: Domeless cubic prayer hall recalling the Kaaba, raised on a broad podium in the city centre.

name: Bitexco Financial Tower
key_features: Tapering glass tower shaped like a lotus bud, with a helipad cantilevered from its upper floors.

name: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park
key_features: Tilted park that gathers rainwater into wetlands and a retention lawn to ease city flooding.

name: Ankara Railway Station
key_features: Symmetrical Art Deco station whose entrance is a tall hall framed by square piers.

name: Civic Center of Lima
key_features: A tall exposed-concrete tower and lower blocks set around raised plazas and terraces in central Lima.

name: Aéro-Habitat
key_features: Slab blocks of duplex apartments on a hillside with interior streets and a shopping level part-way up.

name: Jeevan Bharati Building
key_features: Two red sandstone and glass blocks linked by a giant pergola that frames a plaza on Connaught Place.

name: Bavinger House
key_features: Rough stone wall spiralling up around a central mast that hangs the roof by cables; demolished 2016.

name: Santa Maria Immacolata, Longarone
key_features: Rebuilt after the 1963 Vajont flood: a concrete church whose roof is a curved open-air amphitheatre.

name: 4x4 House
key_features: Four-storey concrete tower on a 4 x 4 m plot by the sea; the top-floor cube is shifted 1 m toward the water.

name: Amorepacific Headquarters
key_features: A near-cube wrapped in vertical sun screens, with large openings cut into three faces as raised gardens.

name: MALBA, Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires
key_features: Stone-clad blocks and glass volumes round a tall central atrium crossed by escalators.

name: The Opus
key_features: A glass cube with a free-form void carved through its middle, splitting it into two towers joined above and below.

name: Baku Crystal Hall
by: gmp Architekten (von Gerkan, Marg and Partners)
key_features: Arena on the Caspian shore wrapped in a faceted membrane skin that lights up at night.

name: Chorsu Bazaar
key_features: Huge blue-tiled dome over the main market hall, a modern take on the domed bazaars of Central Asia.

name: Arvo Pärt Centre
key_features: Low concrete-and-glass building threaded among pine trees, with a slim lookout tower above the forest.

name: MUSAC, Museum of Contemporary Art of Castilla y León
key_features: Plan of repeated square and rhomboid cells; coloured glass facade drawn from León Cathedral's stained glass.

name: Study Pavilion, TU Braunschweig
key_features: A light steel frame of open, fully glazed study floors with outside stairs, built to be taken apart.

name: Baťa's Skyscraper (Building 21)
key_features: 16-storey concrete-frame office tower; the director's 6 x 6 m office was an air-conditioned lift.

name: Estadio Azteca
key_features: Concrete bowl ringed by a frame of raking columns, host of the 1970, 1986 and 2026 World Cups.

name: Most SNP (UFO Bridge)
by: Arpád Tesár, Jozef Lacko, Ivan Slameň
key_features: Asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a 303 m span hung from one leaning A-pylon, topped by a saucer-shaped restaurant.

name: Onagawa Station
key_features: White membrane roof like a seabird's spread wings over a timber lattice; a public hot-spring bath upstairs.

name: Shiroiya Hotel
key_features: A renovated 1970s hotel paired with a new Green Tower: a grassy mound planted with shrubs and trees.

name: Seinäjoki City Hall
key_features: Council chamber clad in dark-blue tiles, reached by grass-and-timber steps climbing the slope.

name: Tautra Mariakloster (convent)
key_features: Cistercian convent on a fjord island: slate-clad walls and lattice glass-and-timber roofs, near medieval ruins.

name: Beijing Railway Station
key_features: Long station front with two clock towers and pavilion-roofed turrets, blending Chinese roofs with socialist realism.

name: Coliseu do Porto
key_features: Streamlined theatre front with a stepped corner tower and a tall vertical sign.

name: AAMI Park (Melbourne Rectangular Stadium)
key_features: 'Bioframe' roof of geodesic domes over the stands, letting light through to the pitch.

name: Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū
key_features: Competition-won gallery with a rippling wall of glass at its entrance; built to ride out earthquakes on a raft slab.

name: La Grande Borne
key_features: Curved serpentine blocks built 1964-71, with colourful, irregularly shaped public spaces residents can identify with.

name: Grande halle de la Villette
by: Jules de Mérindol, Louis-Adolphe Janvier; Bernard Reichen, Philippe Robert (1985)
key_features: 250 x 85 m cast-iron and glass cattle hall, restored in 1985 as a cultural centre.

name: Biosphere (Bigo)
key_features: Glass-and-steel sphere 20 m across weighing 60 tonnes, with movable sails that shade it from the sun.

name: Central Bank of Ireland, Dame Street
key_features: Ireland's only suspended structure building, eight floors hanging from central concrete cores.

name: Blenheim Palace
key_features: Country house with a monumental triumphal-arch East Gate and low corner towers crowned with belvederes of massed stone.

name: Áras an Uachtaráin
key_features: Official residence of the President of Ireland with a garden-front portico said to have inspired the White House.

name: Chichester Festival Theatre
key_features: Grade II* listed Brutalist theatre set in Oaklands Park.

name: Bord Gais Energy Theatre
key_features: Ireland's largest fixed-seat theatre, 2,111 seats, designed by Libeskind for the Docklands.

name: Ames Free Library
key_features: Richardson library beside his Oakes Ames Memorial Hall in North Easton.

name: Campbell Sports Center
key_features: Gateway to Columbia's Baker Field: "points on the ground, lines in space", with external stairs and terraces.

name: Crawford Manor
key_features: Fifteen-storey public-housing tower, a mature Rudolph work and fine local example of Brutalism.

name: Wiesner Building (MIT Media Lab)
key_features: Box-like building with a gridded skin of white modular metal panels; exterior designed with artist Kenneth Noland.

name: Edmonton City Hall
key_features: Designed by Dub Architects and completed in 1992 to replace the 1957 city hall.

name: Rogers Centre
key_features: Retractable-roof stadium that opened in 1989 as SkyDome.

name: Tuschinski Theatre
key_features: Façade blends Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Jugendstil and Amsterdam School styles; two towers flank the western front.

name: Müpa Budapest (Palace of Arts)
key_features: Concert hall and museum complex; the Bartók Hall is 25 m high, 25 m wide and 52 m long. Opened 2005.

name: Baan Dam Museum (Black House)
key_features: Lanna-style buildings with steeply pitched tiered roofs mixed with unconventional contemporary structures.

name: Cathay Building
key_features: 11-storey block with an air-conditioned 1,300-seat cinema, the island's first.

name: Atarim Square
key_features: Brutalist square built from 1971; lower level holds parking and a gas station.

name: Chords Bridge
key_features: Single 118 m mast holds the roadway with 66 steel cables; carries light rail and pedestrians.

name: Royal Tank Museum
key_features: A glass dome at the centre suspends a Cobra attack helicopter; inaugurated 29 January 2018.

name: Brasília Planetarium
key_features: Brutalist concrete building like a flying saucer, with sixteen faces for the compass points.

name: Carrasco International Airport
key_features: New terminal with separate arrivals and departures floors and a top-floor viewing area.

name: Edificio Comega
key_features: First reinforced-concrete skyscraper in Argentina, clad in travertine.

name: La Plata Cathedral
by: Pedro Benoit, Ernesto Meyer, Emilio Coutaret
key_features: Neo-Gothic cathedral with towers about 112 m high, finished in 1999.

name: Catedral de San Agustín de Talca
key_features: Catholic cathedral on Talca's Plaza de Armas, consecrated 30 September 1954.

name: Sunethra Bandaranaike House
key_features: Bawa's conversion of old stables into a house with a new wing, forming an L shape; built 1983-87.

name: Singha Durbar
by: Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana
key_features: Rana-era palace built in 1908, described as a unique merging of building traditions.

name: Alte Feste
key_features: Fort with an inner courtyard, high walls and four towers; the oldest surviving building in Windhoek.

name: Aichi International Arena (IG Arena)
key_features: Multi-purpose arena opened in July 2025, replacing the 1964 Aichi Prefectural Gymnasium.

name: Baldwin Hills Village (Village Green)
by: Reginald D. Johnson; Wilson, Merrill & Alexander; Clarence S. Stein
key_features: A car-free superblock: low garden apartments face large shared greens, with garages kept to courts at the edge.

name: Cathedral Basilica of Lima
by: Francisco Becerra, Juan Martínez de Arrona, Juan Rher, Matías Maestro
key_features: Metropolitan Cathedral of Lima, completed 1797, the oldest and largest church in Peru.

name: Beijing Television Cultural Center (TVCC)
key_features: A continuous lobby gives access to a 1,500-seat theatre and public facilities under one folded volume.

name: Hangzhou Olympic Sports Expo Center
key_features: Exterior drawn from silk texture and the Qiantang River: 28 large and 27 small petal-like steel forms.

name: Beijing National Indoor Stadium
by: Glöckner³ with Beijing Institute of Architectural Design
key_features: Form likened to a traditional Chinese folding fan, hence the nickname 'the Fan'.

name: Community of Christ Temple (Independence Temple)
key_features: Spiralling temple at the Community of Christ headquarters, dedicated 17 April 1994.

name: Akron Art Museum (Knight Building)
key_features: Opened 2007: a three-storey glass 'Crystal' lobby, a 'Gallery Box' and a 327 ft cantilevered 'Roof Cloud'.

name: Basilica of the Fourteen Holy Helpers (Vierzehnheiligen)
key_features: Late Baroque basilica; Neumann split the interior into three ovals, the Mercy Altar marking the apparition site.

name: Bergen Kunsthall
key_features: Early functionalist art hall designed in 1935.

name: Church of the Holy Spirit, Wolfsburg
key_features: Lutheran church and parish centre; design completed and building started in 1961.

name: 2 Columbus Circle
key_features: Edward Durell Stone's modernist building, redesigned by Brad Cloepfil for the Museum of Arts and Design.

name: Güell Pavilions
key_features: Gaudí's early Catalan Modernist gatehouses and pavilions for the Güell estate, built 1884–1887.

name: Trinity Church (Boston)
key_features: Richardson's 1877 church in Boston's Back Bay, home of an Episcopal parish founded in 1733.
